claim.quote: From the 90% confidence limit on the latter a limit is derived on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross-section versus particle mass with a minimum at 1.1 × 10−6 pb.

name: First limits on nuclear recoil events from the ZEPLIN I galactic dark matter detector
notes: Astropart. Phys. 23 (2005) 444 (Alner et al.). The paper itself is not on arXiv; the abstract was read from a university repository record. A published critique (astro-ph/0512120) and reply (astro-ph/0701859) exist.

summary.plain: ZEPLIN-I reported its first results after three runs: no significant population of short pulses that would indicate dark matter. Other physicists later disputed how strongly the method could separate signal from background.
summary.technical: Three runs totalling 293 kg d fiducial exposure with a 3.2 kg fiducial liquid xenon target at 2800 mwe; neutron calibration shows nuclear recoil pulses with a time constant about 0.5 that of gamma and beta events; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limit with a minimum at 1.1e-6 pb. The discrimination claim was disputed in astro-ph/0512120 and answered in astro-ph/0701859.

title: First limits on nuclear recoil events from the ZEPLIN I galactic dark matter detector
why_it_matters: The first published limit from the ZEPLIN programme.
